## How much city fits into ten minutes?

Start at Fountain Square, give everyone the same ten minutes, and change the way they travel. Walking holds close to downtown Cincinnati. Cycling extends the envelope across the Ohio River to the northern Kentucky riverfront. Driving opens a much larger, irregular territory along the road network. All three panels use the same projected extent and scale. The small walking shape is part of the comparison, so I have resisted enlarging it to fill its panel.

For Day 7, “10 minute map” means ten minutes of travel. These are **isochrones**, contours of equal modelled travel time, with a brighter five-minute region inside each ten-minute envelope. The contours follow a routing network rather than a circle drawn around the start. The river, access rules, connections and road speeds help determine their shape.

## Method

The routing experiment uses [Valhalla's isochrone service](https://valhalla.github.io/valhalla/api/isochrone/), hosted by [FOSSGIS](https://valhalla.github.io/valhalla/start/introduction/). The three requests use `pedestrian`, `bicycle` and `auto` costing, with the same OSM Fountain Square coordinate, outward travel, and five- and ten-minute budgets.

Walking uses a 5.1 km/h baseline. Cycling uses a hybrid bicycle with an 18 km/h flat-road baseline and `use_hills = 0.25`, a preference for avoiding steep routes where alternatives exist. These are model settings, not measurements of a particular traveller. Other costing defaults come from the recorded server version. Driving sets `speed_types = []` to exclude live and predicted traffic speed sources, leaving static road speeds. It does not include finding the car, parking search, or the walk from parking to a destination.

Valhalla snaps the input to eligible network locations for each mode. The saved [snap table](origin-snaps.csv) records offsets of 14–40 metres. Those offsets are not extra walking legs added to the driving budget. The cross marks the common requested origin, not every snapped candidate.

The headline distances are the farthest **straight-line extents** of the ten-minute contours: 0.848 km walking, 2.755 km cycling and 12.292 km driving. They are neither route lengths nor a promise of equal access in every direction. The [summary table](summary.csv) records these measurements in NAD83 / UTM zone 16N.

## Data & provenance

The [requests](routing-requests.json) and [contours](isochrones.geojson) were retrieved November 11, 2026. Routing uses OpenStreetMap through Valhalla `3.9.1-9aac4da`; the [source snapshot](source-snapshot.json) records the server's graph timestamp and SHA-256 fingerprints. Map data © [OpenStreetMap contributors](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright), under the Open Database License. A later query can change as the service and graph change; the saved reductions preserve this result.

Background roads and water polygons come from the U.S. Census Bureau's [TIGERweb Transportation](https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/Transportation/MapServer) and [Hydro](https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/Hydro/MapServer) services. They provide geographic context, not the routing graph. Responses are cropped and simplified before plotting. The [acquisition script](acquire-data.R) is the explicit network step; the [R renderer](render-map.R) uses only committed reductions and exports Cairo PNG/PDF files offline.

## What I learned

An isochrone is an envelope around a network calculation. Valhalla derives its contours from a grid and generalizes them here at ten metres, so shaded interiors can contain inaccessible land or water. River polygons are drawn over the fills for legibility; that does not change the routing result. Holes and smaller components are retained.

The driving panel gains reach, but this clock begins at the network. For a short real trip, getting to a car and parking it could consume a substantial part of the same ten minutes. That missing time belongs beside the comparison.

**Alt text:** Three maps compare walking, cycling and driving from Fountain Square at a common scale, with five- and ten-minute envelopes and the Ohio River visible beneath the comparison.
